newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re seeks no long-term Scot Am stake.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re seeks no long-term Scot Am stake.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co and affiliate Securitas Capital will provide Scottish Amicable with capital ahead of a floatation, but the move is not a prelude to taking a long-term stake in the group, a senior Swiss Re official said.
"We have no wish to get involved in ownership or control in any primary insurer," John Coomber, member of executive board at Swiss Re, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Coomber confirmed an announcement earlier on Thursday by Scottish Amicable that it would seek to float its shares on the London Stock Exchange in three to five years time.
Swiss Re and Securitas will provide 395 million sterling.
Swiss Re has just under 60 percent of Securitas. The remaining interest is held by Credit Suisse.
Coomber said that Swiss Re would provide an initial 350 million in reinsurance financing, and the remaining 45 million would come from Securitas.
Coomber did not specify whether the company had set any return targets for the transaction.

"The whole transaction is to facilitate the transition. We are a facilitator," Coomber said, adding that the agreement called for the outside parties involved to exit either at the time of the floatation, or at a later date.
